links.outcome: Effect of prompt engineering and image labeling on accuracy and run-to-run consistency of TI-RADS outputs
links.effect: Modified prompts raised overall consistency (59.5% vs 36%, P<.001) but reduced overall accuracy (45% vs 39.8%, P=.01) and shape/margin accuracy; o3 consistency ranged up to 85.4%.
links.quote: Surprisingly, there was a mixed effect from use of the modified prompt as compared with the basic prompt ( Table 3 ), with poorer consistency for composition (56.2% vs 61.7%, P =.008), but higher consistency for margins (57.5% vs 38.5%, P <.001), echogenic foci (62.9% vs 58.6%, P =.04), and overall TI-RADS classification level (59.5% vs 36%, P <.001).

links.outcome: Accuracy of multimodal LLMs in TI-RADS classification of thyroid nodules
links.effect: Best overall TI-RADS classification accuracy was only 57.3%; authors conclude even the best model output was suboptimal for clinical deployment.
links.quote: The best accuracy obtained for overall TI-RADS classification level was still only 57.3%.

links.outcome: Comparison of three candidate multimodal models (open-source, fine-tuned, commercial) against expert ratings on same data
links.effect: o3 had highest validity (98.6% vs 91.5% LLaVA vs 75% LLaVA-Med) and best accuracy for most components; overall accuracy up to 57.3%.
links.quote: The OpenAI o3 model produced the highest proportion of valid responses (2273/2304, 98.6%), followed by the LLaVA model (2108/2304, 91.5%), then the LLaVA-Med model (1729/2304, 75%, P <.001 for overall comparison).

links.outcome: Output accuracy against expert reference standard for TI-RADS components
links.effect: Overall accuracy was low across models (o3 0.56, LLaVA 0.36, LLaVA-Med 0.35); model outputs were inaccurate against ground truth.
links.quote: The best accuracy obtained for overall TI-RADS classification level was still only 57.3%.

links.outcome: Rate of invalid or uninterpretable responses, including inability to interpret the image
links.effect: 11.6% of responses were invalid (6110/6912 valid); LLaVA-Med valid in only 75%; most invalid due to inability to interpret the image.
links.quote: Most invalid responses were due to the inability of the LLM to interpret the provided image (“I am unable to view the image itself”).
